title: Seoul to Busan: KTX, Express Bus, or Flight Compared
html:
So your Korea trip includes both Seoul and Busan — a smart move, since they feel like two completely different cities. The question is how to get between them. Korea makes this easy: you've basically got three choices — the KTX bullet train, an express bus, or a short flight. Here's how they actually compare, so you can pick the one that fits your trip (and your wallet).

Option 1: KTX (the bullet train)

KTX stands for Korea Train eXpress — Korea's high-speed rail network. It's the fastest way to travel over land, and it's exactly what most Koreans picture when they think "Seoul to Busan." Trains leave from Seoul Station and arrive at Busan Station, both of which are connected to the local subway, so you don't need a taxi on either end.

  • Cost: approx. 59,800 KRW one-way in standard class (first class runs about 30% more)
  • Time: approx. 2 hours 15 minutes on a direct train (some trains stop at Daejeon and/or Daegu, adding 15–30 minutes)
  • Best for: travelers who want speed and comfort and don't mind paying a bit more for it


A KTX-Cheongryong train — one of Korail's newest high-speed models — at Guro Station. Photo: Takeshi Aida, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

A quick tip on the name: not every seat on every train is a "true" bullet-train seat, but for the Seoul–Busan route almost all KTX trains run the whole way at high speed, so you don't need to overthink which one to book.

Option 2: Express bus

If the train feels like overkill for your budget, an express bus (고속버스, "gosok beoseu") is a very solid backup. Buses leave from the Seoul Express Bus Terminal (also called Gangnam Terminal — it's a short walk from Express Bus Terminal Station on subway lines 3, 7, and 9) and arrive at Busan Central (Sasang) Bus Terminal.

  • Cost: approx. 25,000–40,000 KRW one-way, depending on the seat class (standard, premium, or first class)
  • Time: approx. 4–4.5 hours, a bit longer if traffic is heavy
  • Best for: budget travelers who don't mind a longer ride, or anyone who can't get a KTX seat during a busy period


Seoul Express Bus Terminal, where buses to Busan depart. Photo: Kallerna, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Buses on this route run very often — roughly every 30 minutes for most of the day — so you rarely have to plan far ahead. Premium and first-class buses have wider, more reclined seats and fewer seats per row, which is worth the extra few thousand won if you're tall or don't love cramped seating.

Option 3: Domestic flight

You can also fly between Gimpo Airport (Seoul) and Gimhae Airport (Busan), on airlines like Korean Air, Asiana, and Air Busan. The flight itself is short, but don't forget you still need to get to and from both airports.

  • Cost: approx. 30,000–90,000+ KRW one-way — cheap if booked well in advance, pricier if booked last-minute or during a holiday
  • Time: about 1 hour in the air, but budget 2.5–3.5 hours door-to-door once you add security, boarding, and getting to/from each airport
  • Best for: travelers who found a cheap fare, or who are combining this leg with another flight


An Air Busan aircraft at Gimhae International Airport, Busan's domestic airport. Photo: Howon P. Seo, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Because the flight only saves real time if the fare is cheap and you're already near an airport, it's the option most people end up skipping — see the tip below.

How Koreans actually make this choice

Most Korean travelers default to the KTX when they can — it's reliable, comfortable, and by the time you count airport transfers, it's often just as fast as flying, door to door. Students and budget-conscious travelers lean on the express bus instead, since it's roughly half the price and runs so frequently that missing one bus barely matters. Flying Seoul–Busan is fairly rare among locals; it mostly shows up when someone finds an unusually cheap fare or is connecting to another flight.

Booking tips before you go

  • Book KTX seats ahead of time through the Korail app or website, especially if you're traveling on a weekend, a holiday, or around Chuseok (Korean Thanksgiving) or Lunar New Year — those periods sell out fast, sometimes weeks in advance.
  • Express bus tickets can be booked through the kobus.co.kr or bustago.or.kr websites/apps, or bought same-day at the terminal counter if seats are still open.
  • Both Gimpo and Gimhae airports connect to the subway/light rail system, so you don't need a taxi to reach either one — just budget extra time to get there.
  • If your Korean isn't strong, the Korail and bus booking sites/apps do have English options, but a translation app is a handy backup for any prompts that don't switch over.

So which should you pick?

For most first-time visitors, the KTX is the easiest all-around choice — fast, comfortable, and simple to book in English. If you're traveling on a tighter budget or the KTX is sold out, the express bus is a great fallback that runs constantly throughout the day. Flying only really makes sense if you happen to land a cheap fare or you're already connecting through one of the airports.

Quick comparison: KTX vs. express bus vs. flight

Option Cost Time Best for
KTX 59,800 KRW+ ~2h15m–2h45m Speed and comfort
Express bus 25,000–40,000 KRW ~4–4.5 hours Budget travelers, frequent departures
Flight 30,000–90,000+ KRW ~2.5–3.5 hours door-to-door Cheap fares, connecting flights

💬 Trying to decide between the train and the bus for your own trip? Drop your dates in the comments below — happy to help you figure it out!
meta_description: Comparing KTX, express bus, and flights between Seoul and Busan: cost, travel time, and booking tips to help first-time visitors pick the best option.
